who: James J. Hudson, military and Civil War historian at the University of Arkansas; PhD Berkeley, 1952.

evidence.says: University archives identify James J. Hudson as an Arkansas historian, teaching there from 1952 and becoming Graduate School dean in 1972; doctorate from Berkeley in 1952.
LC establishes the heading Hudson, James J.; its source citation identifies the author of The first Blue Yonder (1990).

notes: The fuller name, military aviation subject, university and exact doctorate agree with the supervisor record.

who: Jacob W. Kipp, historian of Russia and Soviet military affairs at Kansas State; PhD Pennsylvania State, 1970.

evidence.says: The 1978 book biography identifies Jacob W. Kipp as associate professor of history at Kansas State, with a Pennsylvania State PhD in 1970.
LC identifies Jacob W. Kipp through his dissertation The Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich and the epoch of the great reforms, PhD Pennsylvania State University, 1970.

notes: Exact doctorate and Kansas State appointment match. The separately listed Miami affiliation was not independently verified.

who: Howard N. Lupovitch, historian of modern Jewish history, formerly at Western Ontario; PhD Columbia, 1996.

evidence.says: The indexed 2013 appointment recommendation gives a Columbia doctorate in 1996, earlier employment at Colby, and the Western Ontario Waks Family Chair from 2009.
The historical society reports his previous Colby and Western Ontario chairs, Columbia history doctorate, and authorship of Jews at the Crossroads.
LC identifies Howard N. Lupovitch, author of Jews at the crossroads, as the Pulver Family assistant professor of Jewish Studies at Colby College.

notes: The university, doctorate and Colby/book connection establish the match. His move to Wayne State was announced in 2013, before the listed students completed.

who: Edward H. Moseley, professor of Latin American history at the University of Alabama, with a history doctorate from Alabama.

evidence.says: Page 6 identifies Edward H. Moseley as Alabama professor of Latin American history and director of International Programs, with all three history degrees from Alabama; his collection emphasized Mexican and Guatemalan history.
LC identifies Edward H. Moseley, contributor to Yucatán in an era of globalization, as emeritus history professor and Capstone International Center director at Alabama.

notes: Institution, field and doctorate institution agree; the sources consulted did not independently establish the 1963 doctorate year.

who: Denise Phillips, historian of science and modern Europe at Tennessee, Knoxville; PhD Harvard history of science, 2004.

evidence.says: Her CV gives Tennessee appointments from 2004, Harvard history of science PhD in 2004, Acolytes of Nature (2012), and PhD advisees Alyssa Culp (2022) and Robert Rennie (2017).
LC identifies Denise Phillips as the author of Acolytes of nature (2012).

notes: Both named students and the exact degree match; the book connects her directly to this authority candidate.

who: Leslie B. Rout, Jr., Latin American historian at Michigan State; PhD Minnesota, 1966.

evidence.says: The scholarly biography gives a Minnesota doctorate in Latin American history in 1966, a Michigan State appointment beginning in 1967, and authorship of The Shadow War.
LC identifies Leslie B. Rout, Jr., author of The shadow war, and explicitly cites the same scholarly biography.

notes: Exact doctorate, Michigan State appointment and the authority record’s cited biography establish the match.

who: Jacques G. Ruelland, historian of science and research supervisor at Université de Montréal; history PhD there, 1994.

evidence.says: His CV gives a Montréal history PhD in 1994, philosophy employment at Collège Édouard-Montpetit, authorship of La Pierre angulaire, and doctoral supervision of Louka Beaudry and Renaud Lippé.
The approval page of Beaudry’s 2013 thesis names Jacques G. Ruelland as directeur de recherche.
LC identifies Jacques G. Ruelland through La pierre angulaire and his philosophy appointment at Collège Édouard-Montpetit.

notes: Direct student evidence and the exact doctorate confirm identity. His CV dates Lippé’s defense to 2012, whereas the AHA entry gives 2016.

who: Jonathan S. Russ, historian of Delaware and modern American business at the University of Delaware; PhD Delaware.

evidence.says: His department identifies Russ as an associate professor with a Delaware PhD and lists Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor, LLP: In Celebration of the First Forty Years (1999).
The university identifies its history professor as Jonathan S. Russ.
LC establishes Jonathan S. Russ from In celebration of the first forty years (1999), whose title page names him with a PhD.

notes: Full name, university, degree institution and distinctive 1999 book agree; the 1996 degree year was not independently confirmed.
